finding: JSON scalar workspace growth released and re-admitted its full size, exhausting fixed stage capacity despite a sufficient largest-workspace allowance. A new regression fails on the baseline with Allocation exceeds admitted stage extent.
contract: Reserve only additional exclusive workspace capacity; merge without pool readmission. Failure preserves the previous reservation in the generic helper; the scalar formatter releases it on failure as before. Materialization and JSON traversal share the helper.
tests: Exact fixed stage and one-byte-below boundaries
Growing scalar siblings through actual JSON sizing with expected UTF-8 byte count
Shared reservation merge rejection releases additional capacity
Invalid workspace extents reject without changing current ownership
Deep traversal and repeated sibling reuse
limitations: Admission units are not exact VM heap storage.
Public JSON encoding includes separate sizing and writing phases; this does not claim that a fixed stage sized only for one phase covers both.
This does not close the historical JSON performance gap versus recursive encoding.
tradeoff: Keep one merged traversal reservation: removes the reservation directory and its depth-proportional live handles, with modeled deep peak reduced from 22,400,256 to 22,080,192 bytes. Two isolated runs show 7–11% slower 20,000-depth encoding; ordinary shapes are mixed. This is a memory/ownership simplification, not a universal speedup. No speculative spare capacity or user tuning is introduced.
